commits.summary: Merge the three cleanup streams: native, jbmc and examples
commits.body:
The reconcile of llm-dlc/loops/cleanup.md (Phase 4, step 1). All three streams had stopped: native blocked on VF-015, jbmc blocked on VF-018 and VF-001 (both for the user), examples done. Each stream's last turns were recorded on its branch, their logs and run records copied into the default workspace, and the three branches merged with the default line. The workspaces cleanup-native, cleanup-jbmc, cleanup-examples and cleanup-integration are forgotten; their directories stay on disk for the user to delete.

Conflicts: only the generated trace files (llm-dlc/index.json, llm-dlc/traces/README.md, llm-dlc/traces/metrics.json, regenerated by this commit) and llm-dlc/README.md, where the default line's application-core sentences and the examples stream's run-record paragraph (VF-013) are both kept. The other files two lines changed (lib/src/equivalence.rs, lib/tests/heap.rs, lib/README.md, examples/index.json) merged cleanly, with independent edits. build.py --index-only marks example 149's page current, since its job passed.

Verified inline at the merge: the lib unit tests (210) and every test binary except integration.rs pass: alignment 34, compare 1, conformance 10 (2 JBMC tests ignored), effects 17, foundations 5 (the integration contract), heap 47 (9 JBMC tests ignored), observations 12, skill 1, summaries 40. integration.rs is left out because its non-ignored tests run JBMC; Phase 4's rerun job runs it at the merge. Every Python suite passes (examples/tools, lib/benchmark, lib/solvers, llm-dlc/tools, verification). test_performance.py failed one test once while cargo was loading the machine, and passed when rerun alone; its output was not kept.

The brief's Progress folds the streams' work: the timebox's one deferral (VF-002's 147 and 148), the three items deferred to the user (VF-018, VF-001, VF-015), and each entry's closing job. Next: step 2, the run records this commit publishes for the first time, then step 3's rerun of the merge's examples.

Out of date in the rest of the brief: 'Where it starts from' describes the state before the streams. VF-015 is no longer the native stream's open item: the user chose llm-dlc/loops/stub-reachability.md (rmvlorrs) to close it after this merge.

commits.summary: prune_workspaces.py: delete jj workspaces only once nothing in them can be lost
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/prune_workspaces.py considers every workspace but the default: those jj lists and the directories of forgotten ones (siblings REPO-* whose .jj/repo points here). It reports by default and deletes only with --delete. A workspace is clear when: no process has its cwd or a file open inside it, and no unfinished loop owns it (a stream workspace NAME-STREAM while llm-dlc/loops/NAME.md's status is neither done nor blocked); every commit of ::WS@ outside ::INTO (the default workspace's @-, or --into) is empty and undescribed; and every file, tracked, untracked or gitignored, is recoverable. That means its exact content is a blob reachable from INTO, or a file anywhere in the default workspace (hashed only on a size match, so its 12 GB verification/.state costs a walk), or it lies in a gitignored build-output directory (target/, build/, ...). It reads file contents, so edits jj never snapshotted count. A .git pointer file jj 0.47 writes is metadata; a .git directory blocks. --archive DIR copies would-be-lost files out and verifies each copy. Deletion re-checks use, forgets a listed workspace, removes the directory and runs git worktree prune. Claude Code transcripts under ~/.claude/projects are left alone.

Verified by test_prune_workspaces.py, 12 cases on throwaway colocated jj repos: merged and deleted; an unmerged commit, an unsnapshotted edit, a unique gitignored .env (and --archive keeping it), a tracked dir named build, a forgotten dir with a unique file, a process inside, a .git directory, and an unfinished loop's workspace all block; a run record copied into the default under another name and ignored target/ are clear. A report-only run here (13 s) finds 3 of 13 clear (the engine-priorities leftovers examples, jbmc, native). The four cleanup-* are kept while cleanup.md waits on jobs. Blocked: the foundations streams' gitignored run records in loop-summaries/ (alignment, heap, observations, summaries), three trace logs only in the foundations directory, and the integration directory's merge files. Nothing was deleted.

commits.summary: prune_workspaces.py only reports, and prints the delete command for a person to run
commits.body:
Without --delete the script only reports whether each workspace is safe to delete, and ends with the exact command that deletes the safe ones. Where a workspace is blocked only by files found nowhere else, it also prints the --archive DIR form. --delete now takes the workspaces by name and refuses unless a person is at a terminal, the check sync.py's allow approve uses: stdin and stdout are terminals, and CLAUDECODE is unset. It checks the named workspaces again, lists the safe ones and asks the person to type "delete" before forgetting and removing any. --archive writes, so it goes with --delete only.

Verified by test_prune_workspaces.py, now 14 cases. The deleting ones run main() with the terminal check and the prompt patched. New: the report prints the command and deletes nothing; --delete is refused in an agent's shell; --delete needs names; a wrong answer deletes nothing; --archive without --delete is a usage error. On this repo the report prints python3 llm-dlc/tools/prune_workspaces.py --delete examples jbmc native, and the same --delete run from this session was refused, with ../in-the-loop-native still in place.
